components.gap: Hypotheses and source variant not supplied (failure condition: unstated assumption). The entry defines adaptedness (body 18-19) but does not impose it: a martingale is any real process with integrable terms and E(X_{n+1}|F_n)=X_n, and sub/supermartingales replace the identity by an inequality (body 20-26). The held source's definition (Durrett p. 217) requires (i) E|X_n|<infinity, (ii) X_n adapted to F_n, (iii) the conditional relation; condition (ii) is dropped. For sub- and supermartingales the inequality does not imply adaptedness, yet the handbook's own proofs treat it as part of the definition (annex 77 'The case n=m follows from adaptedness'; annex 91 'adaptedness was explicitly assumed'; the adapted-and-integrable checks at annex 35, 104, 124, 150, 412, 559, 586, 734), and the optional-stopping chapter on the same route states it explicitly (optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex 12-13). As written, F_n trivial, X_0=-2-U with U uniform on (0,1) and X_n=-1 for n>=1 meets the stated submartingale conditions, while the n=m case of thm:p15-martingale-conditioning fails on {U<1/2}.

defect_observations.observation: Adaptedness of (sub/super)martingales is used throughout the annex (77, 89-91, 144-150, 218-219, 255-260, 455, 586-587) but is not part of def:p15-filtration-martingale. Imposing it in the definition is the root fix for C001; C006 and C011 additionally need the hypothesis on X stated in their first assertions, which are made for an arbitrary process.

The chapter-wide attribution to Durrett Section 4.2 (pp. 217-224) also covers editorial material that is not on those pages: the stopped sigma-field apparatus and bounded optional sampling (held source Thm 4.4.1 p. 235; Ex. 4.4.2-4.4.4 pp. 238-239). Either mark it as editorial or cite its actual locators.

Not counted as a gap because the walk model's filtration is fixed at body 38.
